report.source_text: The patient received systemic therapy in the Department of Oncology. He received whole brain radiotherapy and intrathecal injection of methotrexate once a week in the first month then intrathecal injection monthly thereafter. The clinical symptom (headache and vomiting) relieved after the third month.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 76-year-old man presented with 2 months of incremental headache, nausea, vomiting, intermittent fever, and cervical rigidity. Initial brain MRI showed no mass lesions. CSF analysis revealed elevated opening pressure, slightly increased protein, mild pleocytosis with mononuclear predominance, and negative initial cytology. Subsequent CSF cytology identified malignant cells characterized by enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei and high nucleocytoplasmic ratios, confirming carcinomatous meningitis. No primary tumor was identified by imaging reports in the evidence provided. The patient received systemic therapy including whole brain radiotherapy and intrathecal methotrexate. Clinical symptoms improved after three months of treatment.
